section: Perspectives in Education · Ch20 — Teacher Empowerment — Deep 3
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: Teacher associations/unions in the professional context primarily aim to:

options.option_text: Represent teachers' collective interests, welfare, and professional development
Discourage teachers from voicing any concerns

explanation: Professional teacher associations advocate for members' welfare, working conditions, and professional growth — a legitimate part of teacher empowerment.

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch20 — Teacher Empowerment — Deep 3
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: A cluster-level resource centre where teachers from nearby schools meet monthly to share teaching experiences and solve common classroom problems reflects which model of teacher development?

options.option_text: Isolated, individual self-study with no interaction
Purely top-down lecture-based training with no discussion

explanation: Cluster Resource Centres (CRCs) support peer-based, collaborative professional development — teachers learning from each other's classroom experiences, a model shown to be more sustainable than one-off top-down training.

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch20 — Teacher Empowerment — Deep 3
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: Genuine teacher empowerment includes granting teachers reasonable autonomy in instructional decisions. This is best balanced with:

options.option_text: Accountability for student learning outcomes and adherence to curricular goals
No accountability whatsoever, regardless of outcomes
Complete removal of any curriculum framework
Total control by external agencies over every lesson detail

explanation: Empowerment (autonomy in method) is meaningfully paired with accountability (for outcomes and curricular alignment) — neither unchecked freedom nor total external micromanagement serves genuine professional growth.
